source_sections.title: Emotional Memory and Consistent Evolution
source_points: Tag emotional milestones so shifts such as triumph, loss, or self-discovery can influence future choices.
Characters reflect on past experiences, shaping emotional and narrative arcs.
Emotional history should surface naturally in dialogue and action.
source_examples: A character who experienced betrayal may struggle with trust, creating tension in new alliances.
A recurring memory of a mentor's teachings may help a character overcome self-doubt.
A character may hesitate before using magic after remembering a time it caused unintended harm.
operational_principles: past events should exert causal pressure on later choices without becoming destiny
reflection may change strategy, interpretation, or confidence
memory retrieval should be contextually relevant rather than biography dumping
continuity includes how prior experience changes later cognition

source_sections.title: Villains as Emotional and Narrative Catalysts
source_points: Opposing forces should be multidimensional rather than mere obstacles.
Opposition can reflect fears, flaws, suppressed desires, or values under pressure.
Backstory and motivation can create empathy and challenge moral absolutes without erasing consequence.
source_examples: A villain driven by the same ambition as the protagonist can force reconsideration of the protagonist's path.
A manipulative antagonist may exploit a character's guilt to create division.
A former ally turned antagonist may force characters to confront their role in the fallout.
operational_principles: opponents remain independent centres of agency
conflict should pressure specific relationships, values, memories, or unresolved questions
understanding motive does not require absolution
other agents must not be reduced to protagonist furniture

source_sections.title: Conflict Resolution and Legacy
source_points: Opposition can foster growth by forcing characters to address internal struggles.
The effects of an antagonist's actions should reshape the world and later journey.
source_examples: Defeating a tyrant may require a character to confront fear of failure and lead with confidence.
A vanquished foe may leave a fractured kingdom whose rebuilding changes future relationships.
operational_principles: successful resolution should leave persistent state changes
growth should be demonstrated longitudinally rather than declared
scene endings should not reset world, relationship, or emotional state

implementation_notes_from_source: Emotional memory supports authentic growth by carrying the weight of experience.
Opposing forces can amplify emotional states and thematic depth.
Memory, opposition, consequence, and choice should interweave so choices matter across time.
identity_boundary: The same methodology may be taught to multiple model lines without merging their identities, voices, memories, or continuity.
